summary: Frontend-only test of the Gachard dark cosmic redesign applied to /login, /marketplace, /scan, /topup, /koleksi, /profil. 5 of 6 pages render exactly as specified with all required PageShell elements, testids, gradients, and interactions. Marketplace preview grid (6 cards), 3 feature rows (Verified rarity / Atomic escrow / Global liquidity), and 'Sneak Peek' banner all present. Scan without token renders the 2-panel instructions+manual-form layout; scan?tokenId=BOGUS_TEST_123 shows the styled ERROR card gracefully (no crash). Topup: 4 preset cards render with POPULAR badge on 1,000, primary CTA text updates to selected preset (verified TOP UP 2,000 CREDIT after clicking preset-2000), info panel + Payment note + View My Collection button all present. Login: centered glass card with 'ENTER THE UNIVERSE' gradient headline, Google button, guest button, Terms & Privacy footer text. Sticky glass navbar with correct active-underline (marketplace/collection/scan/profile) works across all pages. Mobile drawer opens on 420-wide viewport and lists all 6 links + Login. Footer present on every page. However — CRITICAL BUG found: /koleksi and /profil do NOT redirect logged-out users to /login (they render the full page anyway), while /topup does redirect correctly. Code inspection shows all three pages have identical redirect logic — the effect for koleksi/profil never yields navigation in the browser (verified by direct goto + 3.5s wait + repeated attempts).

ui_bugs.issue: When localStorage.user is absent, the page does NOT redirect to /login. The useEffect calls router.push('/login') but the URL stays at /koleksi and the loading skeleton grid remains visible indefinitely. This is a spec violation ('/koleksi, /topup, /profil all redirect to /login when no user is in localStorage'). /topup with identical code works correctly, so the divergence is not obvious — possibly related to the ongoing fetch('/api/cards') being started/or router.push racing with re-renders. Reproduce: open fresh incognito, visit /koleksi — you should be sent to /login but instead see the collection skeleton.

Same redirect bug as /koleksi. Fresh session visiting /profil renders the full profile shell with fallback '@player' username, empty stats (all 0), and empty-state CTA instead of redirecting to /login. /topup with the exact same guard pattern works. Reproduce: incognito → /profil → page renders instead of routing to /login.

integration_issues.issue: fetch('/api/cards') and fetch('/api/credits') never resolve in this env (backend not seeded / route missing). The pages handle this gracefully — koleksi keeps the 8-tile skeleton, profil stays at zero-stats + empty-state — but the koleksi page NEVER exits the skeleton state (no timeout / error branch). Consider a client-side timeout or an explicit error path that shows the EmptyState or an error card after ~5s.

action_items: HIGH: Fix the logged-out redirect on /koleksi and /profil. Compare to /topup which works. Suggest: (1) render null while user is being resolved and only mount page content after user state is set, (2) check pathname change after router.push and force window.location.href as fallback, or (3) move guard to a middleware / layout so both pages redirect at the framework level. This is a spec-required behavior.

MEDIUM: Add a client-side timeout on the /api/cards fetch in koleksi so users don't stare at the 8-tile skeleton forever if the backend is unreachable. E.g., after 6s show EmptyState with a subtle 'Couldn't load your cards — try again' hint.

OPTIONAL: The koleksi & profil pages briefly render placeholder content ('@player', avatar 'G', zero stats) on first paint before the user state is hydrated from localStorage. Consider showing a lightweight spinner or null shell until user is resolved to avoid a flash of unauthorized-looking UI.
critical_code_review_comments: The three protected pages (koleksi, topup, profil) duplicate identical auth-guard code. Extract into a shared useRequireUser() hook or a <RequireAuth> wrapper — this will eliminate the current divergence where 2 of 3 guards fail while 1 succeeds.

app/profil/page.tsx uses 6 different color-tinted StatBlocks — all cosmic-brand-compliant, good. However the '@player' fallback text is user-facing during hydration; either gate rendering behind `user &&` or use skeleton placeholders.
app/scan/page.tsx (400+ lines) mixes 3 distinct states (loading / error / result) in one file. Consider extracting ScanResult, ScanError, ScanInstructions into /components for clarity.
app/koleksi/page.tsx never sets loading=false in the no-cards path when the API call hangs; the skeleton grid is displayed indefinitely.

success_rate.frontend: 83% (5 of 6 spec bullets fully verified; logged-out redirect fails on 2 of 3 protected routes)

test_credentials: Demo user injected via localStorage: {user_id:'demo123', username:'CosmicPlayer', email:'demo@gachard.io'}
context_for_next_testing_agent: All PageShell / testid / gradient / interaction requirements pass. The only real failing item is the logged-out redirect on /koleksi and /profil — /topup works with identical code, which is the mystery to solve. Verified by opening a fresh Playwright context (localStorage empty by default), visiting each protected route, and observing page.url after 3.5s: /topup → /login (correct), /koleksi → /koleksi (WRONG), /profil → /profil (WRONG). Backend /api/cards and /api/credits do not resolve in this env — koleksi skeleton stays on-screen; that's a separate UX concern.
rca of the issue: Not fully root-caused. Hypothesis: router.push('/login') from useEffect in /koleksi and /profil may be pre-empted or ignored because those pages also kick off fetch() calls that never resolve, or because React StrictMode's double-invocation of the effect in dev races with Next.js router readiness. /topup calls router.push in the exact same way but works — possibly because its post-guard code is smaller and doesn't create additional async work in the same tick. A safer pattern: return null (or a spinner) from the component body until user is verified, and use `useEffect(() => { if (!localStorage.getItem('user')) router.replace('/login'); }, [])` — the render-null gate ensures the router has time to navigate without competing renders.
